correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, the fixed–free T eigenbasis has q_s=(2s−1)π/(2n+1) and positive simple spectrum. Ground and bond damping vectors vanish on a mode exactly when N|p(2s−1) and N|(2b−1)(2s−1), respectively; Bézout yields N/g|(2s−1). Positive damping implies energy dissipation; the protected subspace and its complement are invariant, and the complement has no imaginary-axis eigenvalue, hence decays exponentially at each fixed set of parameters. The local velocity-kick energy equals the diagonal of the protected projector, evaluated by an elementary complete sine-square sum. Totient placement counts use residue pairing. Verified independent finite diagnostics pass 6,478 mode-index, 238 site/bond spectral, 390 mixed spectral, 79 totient and 31,950 local-kick projector assertions. Computations are corroboration only, not the all-size proof.

value.rationale: Multiple viscous damper placements and physical placement (ground versus between masses) are central design features of finite vibration chains. The theorem gives a complete exact non-asymptotic stability/no-dark-modes decision independent of loss strengths, a precise arithmetic identification of which two physically different damping patterns have identical protected spectra, and a sharp site-by-site asymptotic retained-energy rule after localized excitation. It resolves a concrete optimal-site placement count and guarantees end-bond damping stabilizes. It generalizes prior single-site frequency-locking to joint damping in a mathematically motivated way; it is not solely a numerical recomputation or an arbitrary parameter slice. Limits: linear, homogeneous, fixed–free boundary; no sharp decay constants or nonlinear claims.
